pattern.top_pattern: TX DSNP acute hospital admissions are the main paid-cost driver
key_driver_codes: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections with MCC
Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC
pattern.pattern_details: TX DSNP HMO acute hospital spend is the clearest real cost trend in the analysis and is driven first by more admissions, with some added pressure from higher paid and allowed per admit. The signal is concentrated in authorization-required acute hospital claims, so the most likely lever is inpatient utilization management rather than broad product repricing alone.
pattern.why_it_matters: This is the largest actionable medical cost increase in the analysis after removing validation-only noise.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Run a TX DSNP HMO inpatient management workup focused on admission growth, authorization effectiveness, and recurrent urinary infection stays in acute hospitals.
evidence_summary: TX DSNP HMO acute hospital spend rose $34.7M, driven by 1,628 more admissions and 1,920 more claims.
In the main TX acute hospital signal, average paid per admit rose about $441 and average allowed per admit about $544.
A related TX DSNP HMO acute hospital cluster added another $1.0M, including 45 more urinary infection admissions and paid per admit up about $11.5K on with-MCC cases.
